item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The published manifesto presented López Obrador’s vows to uplift poor and Indigenous communities and provide jobs and welfare, and was described as the foundation of his proposed progressive political program.","notes":["The excerpt supports these stated vows and the manifesto’s described role, but does not directly attribute reducing corruption, violence, and injustice as goals of the program; that wording appears in an endorsement describing his political aspiration."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Mexico was listed among the authors of the 2023 UN draft resolution on the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons; the record identifies it as A/C.1/78/L.24, dated 9 October 2023.","notes":["The excerpt explicitly lists Mexico among the authors, but does not use the term co-sponsor for Mexico in the main record."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0040-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
